full_judgment:
2. The facts as stated in the Writ petition are that, the complainant respondent No.2 Mohammad Iqbal instituted a Criminal Case under section 5(2) of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 before the Chairman, 3rd Labour Court, Dhaka (respondent No.1) against the petitioners for their conviction as they failed to pay the subsistence allowance to the aforesaid respondent No. 2 for 72 days. The said respondent alleged that he was suspended by the authority of Dainik Janata and he being a 'Worker' is entitled to get the subsistence allowance during the period of his suspension. The petitioners by filing supplementary affidavit stated that the respondent No. 2 joined the Dainik Janata as a Senior Accountant on 1-6-84 and he was promoted in the post of Deputy Chief Accountant on 1-10-88 and thereafter he was further promoted to the post of Chief Accountant on 1-12-89 and held that same post till his suspension on 29-10-92. 

 3. Both the petitioners as accused persons were charged with an offence punishable under section 20 of the Payment of Wages Act 1936 and to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence was that the respondent No.2 being the Chief Accountant had managerial and administrative function over his subordinate staffs in the accounts department and thus was not a worker within the meaning of the Labour Law. The respondent No. 2 did not apply for suspension allowance. The criminal case as filed by the respondent No.2 is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The respondent No. 2 resisted the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition and Supplementary Affidavit-in-opposition denied the averment made in the petition and stated that his function was not managerial or administrative in nature. It is not the post but by the nature of job he is a worker. The respondent No. 2 further stated that the petitioners could not prove that the respondent No. 2 had to perform any managerial, administrative or supervisory functions in the establishment. The terms and conditions of such appointment and promotion as contained in those letters as well as in the award of the Wage Board 1986 could not prove that the respondent No. 2 was at all entrusted or vested with any power which is administrative, managerial and supervisory in nature. Although the rank of respondent No. 2 is of Chief Accountant but the nature of job is purely clerical in nature. 

 7. Mr. Ashram Ali Kazi, the learned Counsel for the respondent No. 2, on the other hand, contended that whatever functions the respondent No. 2 had to do were all clerical in nature although he held the post of the rank and status of a Chief Accountant. He argued that there was nothing on record to show that the respondent No. 2 was entrusted to or vested with any power which is administrative, managerial or supervisory in nature. The learned Labour Court having considered the materials on record rightly passed the impugned order of conviction and sentence against the petitioner which is legal and with lawful authority. 

 9. By showing the decision or award of the 5th Wage Board Award 1997 for the Newspaper Employees as published in Bangladesh Gazette dated of 29th May, 1997 in pursuance of the provision of Regulation No. 11(1) of Newspaper Employees (Conditions of Service) Act 1974, vide Annexure-1 of the respondent's affidavit-in- opposition, Mr Ashraf Ali Kazi has tried to argue that there was nothing to show that the respondent No. 2 was at all entrusted to or vested with any power which is administrative, managerial or supervisory in nature. Mr Taimur Alam Khondker has also relied upon the said Annexure-1 and drawing our attention to the 4th chapter of the said gazette notification argued that the respondent No.2 holds office as grade 1 officer and head of the accounts department and under him there are other officers of the accounts department namely, deputy chief accountant and senior accounts officer. The function of the respondent No. 2 as Chief Accountant has been enumerated in said Annexure- 1 which are as follows: 

 From the above mentioned function Mr Khondaker Taimur Alam argued that the respondent No.2 has been vested with the power of managerial and supervisory nature and by no stretch of imagination the respondent can be termed or called a worker, we find substance in his above submission. 

 10. Mr Taimur Alam Khondaker by referring to the contents of the Annexure D and E series of the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner contends that the respondent No. 2 since his suspension was a senior grade officer and he was vested with power to control and supervise the function of his subordinate officers and staffs of the accounts department of the Dainik Janata. From perusal of the Annexure-D and E series we are satisfied that the respondent No. 2 acted in his administrative, managerial and supervisory capacity and by no stretch of imagination he is to be called a worker. Furthermore, we find from the Annexure-F to the effect that one Mr Syed M Reza, a General Manager of the Dainik Janata, a grade 1 officer, also filed a Criminal Case No. 17 of 1993 against the petitioners before the Labour Court under section 20 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the Labour Court acquitted the, petitioner holding that the complainant General Manager is not a worker. In view of what has been discussed above and the materials on record we find that the Labour Court (the respondent No.1) has totally misdirected itself in passing the impugned judgment against the petitioners and the findings made therein are liable to be set aside.
